description: Shared correctness fixtures for the five variants (scalarBaseline, autoVectorizedCandidate, explicitSimd, misalignedInput, smallTailHeavyInput) over four datasets. Vectorization strategy changes ns/element and vector instructions, never the result.

semantics.xorshift64: x ^= x << 13; x ^= x >>> 7 (unsigned/logical); x ^= x << 17 (64-bit wrapping, unsigned interpretation throughout)

sumMinMax.result: sum (wrapping 64-bit), min, max over all elements

thresholdFilter.result: count of elements strictly greater than threshold

dotProduct.fields: a[i], b[i] = xorshift64 stream unsigned-mod 1,000 each (small integers, exactly representable as f64, so summation order never changes the bit-exact result)
dotProduct.result: sum(a[i] * b[i]) over all elements, as f64 (exact, no rounding, given the value ranges)

byteClassification.fields: value = xorshift64 stream unsigned-mod 256 (full byte range)
byteClassification.result: count of bytes in the printable-ASCII range [0x20, 0x7E] inclusive

semantics.smallTailHeavyInput: the same generators, truncated to the first 17 elements (a value not a multiple of any common vector width, so the tail dominates)
semantics.misalignedInput: the same full-length arrays, processed starting at element offset 1 instead of 0 (n-1 elements), so vector loads start at a position not aligned to the vector width's natural array-start alignment
